clue.text: Bridge player engrossed by word games causes quarrel

indicators.note: to be engrossed by something is to be absorbed inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: puzzles like this one are word games
South is one of the four players at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A card player gripped by puzzles ends up starting an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The S sits between CROSS and WORDS, turning CROSSWORDS into CROSS SWORDS; bridge players are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords with someone is an idiom for arguing or clashing with them.

clue.text: Filled with emotion, liaisons involving English ambassador's deputy

indicators.note: something involving another thing takes it in, so a letter is wrapped inside

blocks.note: an emotionally charged moment is full of feeling
love affairs are liaisons
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An emotional diplomat's assistant caught up in romantic entanglements.
explanation.walkthrough: The French spelling of the answer's second word is what lets the English letter be slipped into the familiar word for liaisons.
explanation.definitionFit: A chargé d'affaires is a diplomat who stands in for an absent ambassador, heading the mission.

clue.text: Indecent, old boy on location

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
the scene of a crime is its location

explanation.surface: A former pupil is caught being lewd in some public spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene and indecent are synonyms, both describing what offends public standards of decency.

clue.text: Poles entering track, leaving backer

indicators.note: things entering something go inside it

blocks.note: a spoor is an animal's track or trail
the two poles are North and South

explanation.surface: Explorers heading into the trail abandon whoever funded their expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: NS goes into the middle of SPOOR, giving SPO-NS-OR. 'Leaving' looks like part of the story but simply joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor is someone who supports a person or event, usually financially, as a backer does.

clue.text: Up in Somerset, we ran new resort town

indicators.note: making something new means reshaping it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker reports going for a run while staying in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly the answer is in Somerset, the English county named in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Weston-super-Mare is a seaside resort town on the Bristol Channel coast of Somerset.

clue.text: Let in again to study with German

blocks.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed back into a college to work alongside a German.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit is to allow entry once more, for example to a hospital or a club.

clue.text: Control the movement of bullock

blocks.note: first meaning: to guide or direct, as with a vehicle
second meaning: a young castrated bull

explanation.surface: A farmhand herds a young bull.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both a verb for guiding a vehicle's direction and a noun for a young castrated male bovine.

clue.text: Highest money for people in authority

blocks.note: the top is the highest point
brass is informal British slang for money

explanation.surface: The best pay goes to those in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass is northern English slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Top brass is an informal term for senior officers or leaders, those holding the most power.

clue.text: Spinner - pride shattered after first of sixes

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
something shattered is broken into pieces that land in a new order

blocks.note: the initial letter of the word sixes
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler's confidence is wrecked after being hit for six repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the shuffled letters behind the S, so it is read in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins silk to build its web, so it is literally a spinner.

clue.text: Harps on about children like Annie?

indicators.note: about can mean around in a jumble, so the letters are moved round

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone goes on and on about kids in the vein of a famous musical heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Orphan Annie is the comic-strip and musical character; the question mark flags definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie of the musical is a parentless child, so she is an example of the class named.

clue.text: Treading the boards, using one leg after another

blocks.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so a leg can be ON
a stage of a journey is one leg of it

explanation.surface: An actor walking about the set, putting one foot in front of the other.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket calls the leg side of the field the on side, so 'another' leg is a second word for leg, and 'one leg' follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread the boards is an idiom for acting in the theatre, which is performing in front of an audience.

clue.text: How graduates gained success at university, a little at a time?

definitions.text: How graduates gained success at university

blocks.clueFragment: How graduates gained success at university
blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: graduates succeed by means of their qualifications
second meaning: gradually, step by step

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical literal reading of the phrase; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for gradual change, proceeding in small increments rather than all at once.

clue.text: Sea-ear daughter removed from window

indicators.note: removed from means taken out of, so one letter drops away

blocks.note: a dormer is a window projecting from a sloping roof
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A girl takes a seashell off the windowsill.
explanation.walkthrough: Sea-ear is another name for the abalone, a shellfish eaten in the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is an edible mollusc, also known as abalone or sea-ear, from its ear-shaped shell.

clue.text: Reduce the length of a card game

blocks.note: taken as written
bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: Shortening a game of cards that has gone on too long.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a book or speech is to shorten it while keeping its substance.

clue.text: Rice dish recipe for starters - it's too complicated

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so only the opening letter is used
complicated suggests something tangled, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the initial letter of recipe
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook complains that the instructions for the first course are too fiddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Open University going on about orchestral piece

blocks.note: overt means done openly
standard abbreviation
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A distance-learning college keeps on talking about a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Open University looks like one name, Britain's distance-learning university; it must be split into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an instrumental introduction to an opera or a standalone concert work for orchestra.

clue.text: Steal tin - perplex bishop, leaving

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
to baffle is to perplex
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A thief pockets some tin, confusing a departing cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess notation gives B for bishop; 'leaving' tells you to drop it from the word for perplex.
explanation.definitionFit: To snaffle is informal British for grabbing or pinching something, often quickly.

clue.text: Having a mistress, about fifty, is typical of the person mentioned

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: a mistress is a lover
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A man of around fifty keeping a mistress is just what you would expect of him.
explanation.walkthrough: L slips in after the A of A LOVER. The definition plays on the phrase 'that's him all over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is him all over means it is characteristic of him, exactly his way of behaving.

clue.text: Pick artist to portray the sister of Orestes

blocks.note: to elect is to pick or choose
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A theatre director chooses a painter to play a role from Greek tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Electra and her brother Orestes avenged their father Agamemnon by killing their mother.

clue.text: Chief beginning to split up British Army corps

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the initial letter of split
taken as written
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: The head of a military unit faces the start of its break-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme and chief both mean highest in rank or authority, as in supreme commander.

clue.text: Copy upset clients

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters change position

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Imitating others has annoyed the customers.
explanation.definitionFit: To stencil is to reproduce a design by painting through a cut-out template, a way of copying it.

clue.text: Number carried by sleigh, typically

indicators.note: what is carried by something is held inside it, so the letters sit within the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: How many presents would Santa's sleigh usually take?
explanation.definitionFit: Eighty is a cardinal number, eight tens.

clue.text: Tropical American tree resin, reduced

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: balsam is an aromatic resin from certain trees

explanation.surface: Sap from a rainforest tree is boiled down.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a fast-growing tree of Central and South America, known for its very light wood.

clue.text: Live down under

blocks.note: to be is to exist or live
feeling down is feeling low

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' looks like Australia, but the phrase must be split.
explanation.definitionFit: Below and under are synonyms, both meaning at a lower position than something.

clue.text: Look smart in plant

blocks.note: to eye something is to look at it
a bright child is a smart one

explanation.surface: Appear well dressed in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small flowering herb, Euphrasia, once used to treat eye complaints.

clue.text: Young animal allowed outside at all?

indicators.note: a word placed outside another surrounds it

blocks.note: to let is to allow
ever means at all, as in 'if ever'

explanation.surface: Was the creature ever let out?
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a hare in its first year, a young animal of that species.

clue.text: Prattle about milliner

blocks.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
a milliner makes hats, as a hatter does

explanation.surface: Idle talk concerning a hat-maker, perhaps the Mad Hatter's tea party.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatter and prattle both mean light, rapid, trivial talk.

clue.text: Quarrelsome conversation if male drunk? I can't express how I feel

definitions.text: I can't express how I feel

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about unsteadily, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: to have words is to argue
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An exasperated listener to a tipsy man's rows is left speechless.
explanation.definitionFit: Words fail me is an idiom said when one is too shocked or moved to find anything to say.
